newsitem.title: USA: Buba's Jochimsen -- good conditions for stable rates.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Jochimsen -- good conditions for stable rates.

text.p: German Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said he expects solid economic conditions to prevail over the long term in his country, enabling interest rates to remain steady.
Speaking at a luncheon sponsored by the American Council on Germany here, Jochimsen said, "I see that we will have good conditions for a long time to continue stable interest rates."

When asked about the possibility of Germany easing official interest rates, Jochimsen said: "As of the moment I see no necessity to think of moving downwardly further. We are not in a Japanese situation."
Turning to the outlook on prices, Jochimsen said, a rise in prices is not apparant at the moment in Germany.
"We see no inflation pressures in Germany right now. We are quite comfortable at 1.5 percent," he said.
"If we were to go below 1.0 percent, I would be afraid that it would get deflationary".
Jochimsen did express doubts about the strength of German economic growth.
"What I'm worried about is that our upturn will not be fierceful and strong enough to actually solve...the necessiaty of structural changes," Jochimsen said.
Jochimsen also expressed regret if Britain decides not to join European Economic and Monetary Union.(EMU)
"It would be a shame, and it would be a tragedy if Britain should choose...to stay outside this important event," he said.
"I am rather struck by the kind of self isolation that now is present in Britain," Jochimsen said.

Regarding any delay in the launching of EMU by the planned January 1, 1999 deadline Jochimsen said in his opnion a delay would not be a "catastrophe" and that the financial markets need not have an "explosive reaction".

Turning to the proposed stability pact Jochimsen said: "To my mind, (the stability pact) has to be equipped with speedy and biting sanctions based on a shift of the burden of proof to the sinners so to speak."
